rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the 25 mm tape at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m (0.012 m footprint, which covers the tape width with margin), all at y = 0.04 m ahead of the axle so the robot reads the line before it reaches the wheels. Sensor weights are -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, proportional to sensor x. This makes the signal positive when the line is to the left, which steers left as the contract requires, and it gives a signal scale of about ±2. Controller: base_speed 1.6 (about 80% PWM) to aim for the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving headroom for bends. kp 2.0 gives a moderate correction (turn about 4 at full signal, roughly 1400 PWM differential). ki 0.05 is small, so it can remove steady bias from the motor mismatch without winding up. kd 0.1 adds light damping against oscillation. line_loss 'last_direction' lets the robot recover toward the side it last saw the line. Chassis: wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.8 kg, a moderate, stable inertia. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend with few line-loss events. The main risk is overshoot in the slalom at this speed. Next measurements: rms_error and max_error to check tracking margin against the 0.06 m off-track limit, steering_oscillation to judge whether kd is adequate, and completion_time to see whether base_speed can rise.
